questions.prompt: Which modifier is placed before an adjective to express 'more' (comparative degree, e.g. 'more handsome')?
questions.explanation: 'Mas' expresses comparative degree ('more' / '-er', e.g. Mas gwapo = more handsome).

questions.prompt: In comparative sentences, when comparing against a person's proper name (e.g. 'than John'), which preposition is used?
questions.explanation: 'Kaysa kay' is used before a person's proper name. 'Kaysa sa' is used before common nouns or places.

questions.prompt: Which prefix attaches to an adjective root to express equality ('as [adjective] as')?
questions.explanation: 'Kasing-' expresses equal quality ('as X as', e.g. kasingganda = as beautiful as).

questions.topic: Sound Shift before B and P
questions.prompt: Before root words starting with 'b' or 'p' (e.g. 'bait'), 'kasing-' shifts to 'kasim-'. What is the correct form for 'as kind as'? ______
questions.explanation: Sound shift: kasing- + bait -> kasimbait (the 'n' shifts to 'm' before 'b' or 'p').

questions.prompt: When two subjects are compared side-by-side (e.g. 'Sina Maria at Elena ay ___'), which prefix is used for equal beauty?
questions.explanation: 'Magkasing-' is used when subjects are listed together (e.g. Sina Maria at Elena ay magkasingganda).

questions.prompt: Which prefix expresses 'very' or 'extremely' when attached to an adjective root (e.g. 'extremely beautiful')?
Which prefix forms the superlative degree ('the most' / '-est', e.g. 'most delicious' -> '___masarap')? ______
questions.explanation: 'Pinaka-' forms the superlative degree (e.g. pinakamasarap = most delicious).

questions.prompt: How can an adjective be duplicated with a ligature to express 'very [adjective]' (e.g. 'very beautiful')?
questions.explanation: Duplicating the adjective with a ligature (-ng, -g, na) expresses intensive degree: maganda + -ng + maganda = magandang-maganda.
